title: National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Streamlined Governance) Bill 2019
short_title: National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Streamlined Governance) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would improve how the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 operates by introducing simpler governance arrangements.

Schedule 2 would require the CEO or any officer of the National Disability Insurance Agency, and the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commissioner or any Commission officer, to comply with a formal notice or summons from a Royal Commission to produce documents, information or give evidence, subject only to public interest immunity.
Producing or disclosing information or giving evidence under the Royal Commission requirement would not breach the confidentiality provisions of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013.
changes: Introduce streamlined governance arrangements under the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013.
Require relevant agency and commission officers to comply with Royal Commission notices or summonses, subject only to public interest immunity.
Exempt such compliance from the confidentiality provisions of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013.
summary.affected: The National Disability Insurance Agency, its CEO and officers, the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commissioner and Commission officers, and Royal Commissions.

divisions.question: The majority voted in favour of a motion introduced by Tasmanian Senator [Carol Brown](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/carol_brown) (Labor), which means the words below will be added to the usual second reading motion, which is "*that the bill be [read for a second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/)*" (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). This motion does not make any legal changes in and of itself but is politically influential because it represents the will of the Senate. ### Motion text > *At the end of the motion, add:* > > *", but the Senate calls on the Government to:* > > *(a) remove the average staffing level cap for the National Disability Insurance Agency set out in Part 2 of Budget Paper No. 4 (2019–20); and* > > *(b) directly employ the number of people required to administer the National Disability Insurance Scheme and the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013."*

The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2019-11-13.194.1) introduced by NT Senator [Malarndirri McCarthy](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/nt/malarndirri_mccarthy) (Labor) that would have amended the usual [second reading motion](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/) "*that the bill be read a second time*", which is parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. ### Motion text > *At the end of the motion, add:* > > *", and the further consideration of the bill be an order of the day for the first sitting day after the findings and recommendations of the 2019 review of the NDIS Act and the new NDIS Participant Service Guarantee are publicly released."*

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2019-11-13.191.2) to agree with the main idea of the bill, as amended. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill [for a second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/). This means that they can now discuss the bill in greater detail. ### Main idea of the bill According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd1920a/20bd026): > *The purpose of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Streamlined Governance) Bill 2019 (the Bill) is to amend the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 (NDIS Act) to:* > > * *introduce new requirements for appointments to the Board of the National Disability Insurance Agency (the Agency) and the Independent Advisory Council* > * *establish a 28 day requirement for consultation with host jurisdictions for certain matters and* > * *re-categorise some of the National Disability Insurance Scheme rules (NDIS rules) from Category A and Category C to Category D.*

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2019-11-14.89.1): > *That the committee report progress and ask leave to sit again.* It was introduced by WA Senator [Mathias Cormann](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/wa/mathias_cormann) (Liberal).

speeches.speaker: Bill Shorten
speeches.brief: The speaker opposed the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Streamlined Governance) Bill 2019, arguing it would lower the standard for appointing NDIA board members from requiring all states and territories' support to a simple majority. They cited a University of Western Australia report highlighting the NDIS's $4 billion+ underutilisation, unsustainability, and major gaps in responsibility and funding between governments.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the NDIS Amendment (Streamlined Governance) Bill 2019 to reduce delays in board appointments, criticised the withholding of draft plans from participants, and urged the government to address the exclusion of people who acquire a disability after age 65 from accessing the NDIS.

speeches.speaker: Melissa Price
speeches.brief: The National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Streamlined Governance) Bill 2019 simplifies rule-making and decision-making under the NDIS Act and ensures the Royal Commission into Violence, Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation of People with Disability has clear authority to obtain information from the NDIA and NDIS Commission.
